cands.bio: Democrat representing District 99 in the Alabama House since 2018. Navy veteran. Executive director of Mobile Community Action 1980–87, four terms on the Mobile County Commission, and Mobile's first African-American mayor, serving 2005–2013.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving 2026 voter-guide recommendations from Tabitha's List and from Unburdening The Ballot (both Sway voting groups).

cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or stated positions from Jones on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership by investors or foreigners, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 candidate surveys, and the pages we had list his sponsored bills only as a table with no content. We found no documented public stances on data centers or development, and no controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements beyond two voter-guide listings. The exact years of his county commission service and the dates of his Navy service were not given in the pages we had.

cands.name: Charlie Watts
cands.bio: Republican candidate for Alabama House District 99 in 2026. He advanced from a canceled Republican primary without appearing on the ballot and lost the general election to incumbent Sam Jones (D). No other biographical details were found.
cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Charlie Watts was born or raised, when he came to Alabama, or what he does for work. No prior elected office is documented. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, and we found no campaign site, interviews or questionnaires stating his positions on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, campaign money, policing, guns, abortion or education. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. We found no news coverage of controversies.
